name: Henri Leinonen
title: Associate Professor
affiliation: School of Pharmacy, University of Eastern Finland
shortDescription: Research on retinal plasticity and novel therapeutic approaches for retinal degeneration.
details: Henri Leinonen is a Principal Investigator and Group Leader at the School of Pharmacy, University of Eastern Finland (UEF). He trained in pharmacy (MSc) and completed doctoral research in neurobiology at UEF, followed by postdoctoral training at the Department of Pharmacology, Case Western Reserve University, and the Center for Translational Vision Research at the University of California, Irvine. His research group, established in 2022, integrates retinal pharmacology, drug repurposing, and plasticity-based approaches to counter retinal degeneration and retinal cell stress, with the goal of advancing therapies to address unmet medical needs. His work has been recognized with several competitive distinctions, including an Academy of Finland Fellowship, the FEBS Excellence Award, and the Best Doctoral Thesis of the Year Award at the UEF Faculty of Health Sciences. He serves on the International Scientific Committee of the International Center for Translational Eye Research (ICTER) at the Polish Academy of Sciences and contributes broadly to the academic community through doctoral committee service, external evaluation of dissertations and research funding applications, and participation in academic evaluation processes in Finland and internationally.

name: Grazyna Palczewska
title: Project Scientist
affiliation: Brunson Center for Translational Vision Research & Gavin Herbert Eye Institute, USA
details: Grazyna Palczewska, PhD is a Project Scientist at the Department of Ophthalmology in the School of Medicine. Dr. Palczewska is advancing custom-developed non-invasive, high-resolution two-photon ophthalmoscopy imaging for routine quantitative evaluation of certain biochemical processes within the healthy, disease and therapy impacted retina. She developed and continue advancing assays and equipment to visualize and quantify impact of the retinal therapies and drug candidates on retina preservation. This includes small molecule, antibody bound ligands and gene editing. Her publications in PNAS outlined the road to safe and informative two-photon imaging in humans. This research was crowned with 2022 Journal of Clinical Investigation where she was part of the team that presented first data on two-photon imaging of the retina in human subjects. Furthermore, because exchange of ideas and expertise among scientists from around the globe is crucial for the progress and competitive research she coordinates Ophthalmology Research Seminars, now word-wide recognize seminar series.
